decisions.reason: The bounded significand and exponent ranges did not explicitly require integer k and e. Real k makes the alleged finite set infinite and invalidates its adjacent-grid use. Both indices are now explicitly integral, preserving the intended normal and subnormal grids and all rounding formulas.

The final quotient argument uses x,y for z but must use u,v for the nonzero divisor w. Corrected the coordinates: |w|=0 implies u²+v²=0, hence u=v=0. The earlier identity |w||1/w|=1 also already implies positivity, so this local typo does not invalidate the established quotient conclusion.

Step 4.1 expressly derives storage monotonicity from the greatest-lower/least-upper definitions, rather than claiming it as part of L2. Those actual definitions are linked in the Given supplier and are available through both dependencies. For x≤y the lower candidate sets nest forward and the upper candidate sets nest backward, so both extremal maps are nondecreasing, including the prescribed overflow sentinels. The bisection invariant and grid-transition argument are sound.

A_0 and B_0 denoted absolute sums in step 1.1 but are overwritten by the signed partial-sum notation at N=0 in step 2.1. Renamed the nonnegative absolute sums A_abs and B_abs throughout. The triangular-versus-square finite-sum bound is then bounded by two vanishing absolute tails with fixed nonnegative multipliers; the product-limit estimate completes the unchanged claim.

The geometric derivative series was omitted from the majorant argument. Added the eventual-ratio bound v_(n+1)/v_n=r(1+1/n)≤q<1 for v_n=n r^(n−1), with r=0 handled separately. Geometric tails uniformly dominate the derivative terms on |x|≤r. The factorial and odd-series bounds already establish the remaining unchanged claims.

The actual operation definition specifies extremal directed rounding through def-dyadic-floating-point-format-and-directed-rounding; enclosure alone is not the only available premise. Extremal lower and upper maps are nondecreasing by inclusion of their candidate sets. Thus outward conversion preserves inclusion of exact interval hulls; componentwise natural interval operations preserve rectangle inclusion, and the M_B,m_B bounds prove ball isotonicity. The DAG induction explicitly requires all nodes finite, so no missing soundness hypothesis is used.

The quotient set is unbounded in both directions by the exhibited reciprocal sequence. The example incorrectly listed inconclusive as a permitted real-division branch; the actual operation definition allows split-domain or entire here. Removed the extra status without changing the example or its unboundedness argument; inconclusive remains available only in other specified operation branches.

The schema deliberately permits justified_by results to depend on the procedure they justify; those reverse links are not recursive procedure calls or logical premises of the instructions. The procedure is explicitly specified by finite DAG ordering, rational endpoint arithmetic, fixed series truncations, finite root bisection and finite canonical partitions, with failure statuses for unresolved domains. The cited theorems verify the finite outputs nodewise without assuming their soundness in the definition. No mathematical circularity occurs and no carrier edit is warranted.

The original unconditional machine-enclosure assertion fails for p=2, emin=0, emax=2, f(t)=6t, X=[0,2], c=0, n=1, C0=[0,0], C1=[6,6], D=[0,0]: Nmax=6 and the polynomial product reaches 12 and overflows. Preserved the unconditional analytic Taylor remainder and exact n=0 set-sum claims, and explicitly conditioned the machine certificate on every operation and endpoint conversion being finite. L3 and step 2.1 now retain the actual DAG-soundness hypothesis.

L2 is the arithmetic soundness and isotonicity theorem, not the bisection procedure. Replaced the inaccurate bisection-supplier description with its actual square-root enclosure clause. That clause proves precisely the finite square-root-node inclusion and nesting used here; the local series bounds and canonical-cell arguments handle the other real primitives, and step 3.1 composes the primitive bounds in topological order.

L2 and L3 were restated as generic whole-leaf results although their explicit interfaces name real elementary primitives and complex exp/Log. Replaced those restatements with their precise domains, added the arithmetic and square-root supplier L4, and supplied a topological induction for arbitrary admitted homogeneous typed DAGs, including arithmetic-only outputs. All intermediate results are finite in a successful call and all domain guards have passed. The queue cover, 2B+1 bound and final global-width test then prove the unchanged certificate claim.
